title: WebSocket testing (Robert Koch, 2012 GSoC)
description: The 2012 WebSocket testing project in the Student Hall of Fame, set beside the commits that moved the code out of core and into the websocket add-on.
narrative:
For a proxy used mostly by security testers, WebSocket traffic that could not be seen or edited probably left a gap in testing. The Student Hall of Fame lists WebSocket testing (Robert Koch) as a 2012 Summer GSoC project, and the project wiki says it "aims to adding support for WebSockets to ZAP". A zaproxy commit dated May 2012 created a branch for the work, and a later commit that month merged trunk into it to keep up with changes.

The UI came next: a June 2012 commit added new details to a WebSockets UI panel, including opcode and payload length. These commits were in zaproxy, where the WebSocket code was then part of core.

In January 2013 a zaproxy commit removed the WebSockets add-on, and a zap-extensions commit that same day moved the WebSockets extension out of core. Relocation continued: in April 2016 a commit unloaded components from core, and in April 2019 another relocated the add-on to its own project.

The current zaproxy tree has no file with websocket in its path. The add-on is still in zap-extensions, with 231 commits in its history, and its latest commit, dated September 2026, is titled "websocket: Support GSPM for passive scripts".

chapters.title: 2012: a branch for WebSockets in zaproxy
chapters.text: The Student Hall of Fame lists WebSocket testing (Robert Koch) as a 2012 Summer GSoC project. The project wiki says it "aims to adding support for WebSockets to ZAP" and that "one can see & even edit messages". A zaproxy commit dated 2012-05-07 is titled "create branch for my GSoC project: Enhancing ZAP with WebSockets support." A later commit dated 2012-05-22 is titled "Merged trunk into WebSockets-Branch to keep up changes".

chapters.title: 2012: a UI for WebSocket traffic
chapters.text: A commit dated 2012-06-13 is titled "further refactorings plus new informations in WebSockets-UI-Panel (#, opcode, payload-length)". An earlier commit the same day (da93cc9) is the first of the two to mention user interface classes for displaying WebSockets communication in its subject. These commits are in the zaproxy repository, where the WebSocket code was then part of core.

chapters.title: January 2013: moved out of core
chapters.text: A zaproxy commit dated 2013-01-24 is titled "removed WebSockets add-on (prepared to move over to extensions project)". A zap-extensions commit dated the same day, 2013-01-24, begins "moved WebSockets extension out of core". The current zaproxy tree has no file with websocket in its path.

chapters.title: 2016 to 2019: unloading from core, then its own project
chapters.text: A zap-extensions commit dated 2016-04-26 is titled "websocket: unload components from core". On 2019-04-03 a commit titled "websocket: relocate to its own project" is dated; it is the earliest commit in the history of the addOns/websocket directory.

chapters.title: Where it stands now
chapters.text: The websocket add-on is still in zap-extensions. The latest commit touching addOns/websocket is dated 2026-09-23 and is titled "websocket: Support GSPM for passive scripts". The add-on's history contains 231 commits.
